title: Successful-Only Latency Averaging (Incomplete Average)
pattern: Excluding failed or timed-out transactions from the calculation of average latency.
why_bad: When requests time out or fail, they represent the worst-case performance of the system (often waiting for a maximum timeout threshold). By excluding uncompleted or failed requests, the average latency is artificially skewed downwards, creating a false "all-green" dashboard while users experience infinite hangs.
detection: Look for latency aggregation loops that check for successful status codes or filter out errors before summing the duration.
counterexample: None. Failing to report/account for timeout latency in overall metrics is a major observability gap.
strength: Strong` — structurally hides system degradation by omitting the slowest requests.
source: Michael T. Nygard - *Release It!* (2007), Chapter 13, p. 212.
